Since the appeal is barred by delay of 33 days as such the present application is accompanying the present appeal.
2.
For the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed and delay of 33 days in filing the present appeal is condoned.

3. Disposed of accordingly.
1.

The appellant came to suffer physical injuries on account of road traffic accident which came to take place on 27.10.2022 when the appellant was commuting in vehicle (Baleno) bearing registration No. JK02CB-6919 when it came to be hit by the offending vehicle (Bus) bearing registration No. JK02CS-9533 at Police Check Post Dumi (Jammu-Akhnoor National Highway),
Jammu leaving the persons travelling in the said Baleno car injured.
Number of claim petitions came to be preferred out of this accident before Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu.

sentences.text: 2. With respect to the appellant, his claim for compensation was related to the damages suffered by the aforesaid vehicle (Baleno) of which the appellant was the owner.

3. All the claim petitions preferred before the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu came to be clubbed and dismissed by a common order dated 13.12.2023 holding the claim petitions are barred by limitation as envisaged under amended Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 in terms of amendment carried out by Act No. 32 of 2019 w.e.f. 09.08.2019.
4. The appellant's claim petition was on file No. 66/Misc as the appellant had preferred an application for condonation of delay for seeking entertainment of his claim petition.

5. Thus, finding himself non-suited by the award of Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT),
Jammu, the appellant is invoking the appellate jurisdiction of this Court under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 raising important question of law as to whether the limitation so prescribed under Section 166 of the Act is to get invoked only after the entire mechanism as envisaged under the Act read with the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of "Gohar Mohammad Vs. Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation" was to be carried out and exhausted.

entities.text: Gohar Mohammad Vs. Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that nothing of that sort came to take place in the context of the accident in reference as a result whereof the appellant was left to his own call to approach the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu and for that purpose he could not have been faulted by the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu.
7. Prima facie case is made out.

8. Issue notice to the respondents.
9.
Appellant to furnish registered postal covers for the service of the respondents within seven days whereupon the Registrar Judicial, Jammu to issue notice to the respondents.

In the meantime, send for the record of file No. 66/Misc titled "Abhjeet Singh Vs. Raj Kumar and Ors", bearing date of institution 17.06.2023 and date of decision 13.12.2023 from the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu.
